topic: Hidden senses beyond the five: proprioception, balance, temperature, pain, interoception
hook: 5 senses nobody taught you in school
caption:
Sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch. That list leaves out the sense that lets you touch your nose with your eyes closed, and the one that makes mint feel cold.

Depending on how you define a sense, scientists count far more than five. Part 2 drops tomorrow, so follow for one fact your brain won't believe, daily. Save this for the next time someone says 'sixth sense.'

Which of these would you least want to lose?

Cover: 5 senses nobody taught you in school
🎨 AI-generated image

1/5 Proprioception
Sensors in your muscles and joints track your limbs. It's why you can touch your nose with your eyes closed.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/5 Balance (3)
Fluid in tiny canals in your inner ear moves as you move. Spin, then stop: it keeps sloshing. That's dizziness.
📷 unknown (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

3/5 Temperature (Mint)
You have separate sensors for cold and heat. Menthol triggers your cold sensors, which is why mint feels cool.
📷 Mangosapiens (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

4/5 Pain (0)
Pain has its own sensors, separate from touch. Your brain tissue has none, so surgeons can operate while you're awake.
🎨 AI-generated image

5/5 Interoception
Your sense of inside signals: hunger, thirst, a full bladder, even your own heartbeat.
📷 Dguendel (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia
